en: Did you treat my wounds?

Don't get me wrong. I just didn't wanna
watch you croak. That's it.
Aniki. He's finally awake.
How are you feeling, Lo?
More grateful than anything.

Sorry to ask you this so soon, but I need
to continue our conversation from Little Asia.
Can you talk?
Hold on. I need to make one thing clear first.

I'm a detective, so I wouldn't openly
discuss any crimes you've committed.

That goes double for you, Kiryu.
Understood?

You do whatever you think is
right, Date-san.
We'll accept your judgment here.
Lo. You okay with that?

I no longer intend on
running away from the truth.

First, Lo...
Why did the Saio come to Japan?
And why are you fighting the Tojo Clan?

Lastly, what exactly is the secret of Onomichi?
I need some answers.

Regarding the secret of Onomichi...
The truth of it still eludes me.

What!? That doesn't make a shred o' sense!
Aniki, you really gonna trust this guy?

He's just spewing whatever bullshit
he can to make us doubt Hirose-san!

Calm down, Yuta.
Go on.

The secret of Onomichi was originally crafted
by my father and Chairman Kurusu.
It was a project they planned together.
A project?

Japan was at war with
the rest of the world at the time.

If I had to guess, I would say
the secret was military in nature.
But that was before the Yomei Alliance.

Are you saying Iwami Shipbuilding made this
deal with the previous head of the Saio Triad?
Precisely that.

The first time I heard the secret
mentioned was roughly 1985.

From his deathbed, my father spoke
 of
it being Kurusu's sole political weakness.
He divulged nothing else about it.

But when he died, he left me something he
claimed was the key to uncovering the secret.
The key? And what was it?

A code that apparently leads
somewhere in Onomichi.

But I am no closer to decoding it
today than I was 30 years ago.

30 years ago... That's when
I joined the Tojo Clan.

It was a prosperous time, not only for the
criminal underworld, but society as a whole.

By that point, Heizo Iwami had long established
his new persona: Takeru Kurusu.

In public, he was chairman of Iwami Shipbuilding.
In private, he presided over the Yomei Alliance.

These two diametric extremes allowed him
to establish the role of the Fixer.

Now that you mention it, Kurusu and
the Yomei only rose to power after the war.

It's possible that Onomichi's secret is what got
him involved in crime to begin with.

I cannot comment on Kurusu turning
from the law so many years ago.

However, I knew he had an image to uphold
as the chairman of his successful business.

Nobody could find out that he was actually
running a massive criminal syndicate as well.

That fact allowed me to pressure Kurusu over
the secret of Onomichi my father spoke of.
And to force him into a secret deal with me.
The <font_kind=yakuza_italic>heihaizi</font_kind> smuggling.

Along with the forging of their documents.
In other words, human laundering.
Yes, exactly.

<font_kind=yakuza_italic>Heihaizi</font_kind> are children who exist outside
the awareness of the Chinese government.

They have no documents. No education.
They are born destined for a life of crime.

However, these children knew we could
give them new lives as citizens of Japan.

And in order to grasp that opportunity
,
they willingly indebted themselves to us.

So the only reason you helped them
was for
 the eventual payday.

We are not a charity. We do earnestly
hope to save those children, though.

And if you consider things from their perspective
,
an escape was something only we could offer.

That's all well and good, but how does
Kurusu play into this situation?

His shipbuilding corporation offered us
the ideal smuggling route for <font_kind=yakuza_italic>heihaizi</font_kind>.

He also had ways to bend the Japanese
government to conform to his desires.

As such, Takeru Kurusu was utterly vital
to my human laundering scheme.

So Kurusu was smuggling in illegal immigrants
and forging their documents on top of it all.
He was taking a huge risk.

That should go to show just how important
protecting the secret of Onomichi is to him.

In any case, our deal proceeded
exactly as planned.

After that, I returned to China and ensured the
Saio stayed as far away from Japan as possible.

The goal in this was to limit any chance
of further interaction with Kurusu.

After all, I couldn't risk him catching on to my
bluff regarding the secret of Onomichi.

Then why has your organization
decided to show up in Japan now?

I mean, the Tojo caused that fire in Little Asia
specifically so you'd have room to take root.
And don't even try playing dumb.

That was all orchestrated by
Kurusu's son, Tsuneo Iwami.

He and my son Jimmy went behind
my back to bring the Saio Triad here.

They even managed to ensure Sugai of
the Tojo Clan invited us here personally.

In Kamurocho, the Tojo Clan
will be reborn?

Tsuneo planned on using Sugai and Someya
to make the Tojo Clan into his puppet.

With their help, he would gradually be able
to gain control of the whole of Kamurocho.

The Saio Triad was nothing but
a pawn he used to that end.
And you were in no position to refuse him.

In other words, he turned your human laundering
plot against you. Used the <font_kind=yakuza_italic>heihaizi</font_kind> as hostages.
You know what happened next, Kiryu-san.

At the urging of Tsuneo Iwami, the Saio Triad
staged a fake war in Kamurocho with Sugai.

That was the war which led the police
to arrest the Tojo Clan's sixth chairman.

Once Tsuneo had his puppet, Sugai
,
take the reins of the Tojo Clan...

...My use had expired, and so he
made an attempt on my life.

He was presumably plotting to kill me
from the moment he invited us into Little Asia.

But he wasn't actually able to get to you.
Instead, he killed your son. Jimmy Lo.

From Kurusu's standpoint, Tsuneo's
bloodthirst must have been unsettling.

I assume he feared I would avenge my son's
death by revealing the secret of Onomichi.

That would explain why he had Hirose
pressure me into leaving the country.
And why he offered to return Yuta to me.

That's enough of yer bullshit, old man.
The boss would never do that. I don't believe it!

The secret of Onomichi has become little
more than a curse for Kurusu and Hirose.

That is why they turned my own son, Yuta
,
against me as an assassin.

There is no means too great
to ensure my eternal silence.
You're lying!

And you, Kiryu-san? Can you
bring yourself to doubt Hirose?
Honestly, I owe him a lot for protecting Haruka.

I don't want to think about what would have
happened to her and Haruto without him.

So, I have to agree with Yuta.
I want to trust Patriarch Hirose.
This building has rooftop access, yes?

I would like to speak with you alone
from here forward, Kiryu-san.
I will await you on the roof.
Lo's waiting for you up there.

Don't worry 'bout me, Aniki.
You can go on ahead.

Before you go, Kiryu.
It's about Haruka.
What happened to her?
She's coming back.
Y'serious!?

While you were over in Little Asia, I left
Haruto in the care of the police hospital.

It might be nothing, but a tear rolled
down Haruka's face when he was with her.
I think she's trying her damnedest to wake up.
Thought you could use that bit of good news.
I see. I appreciate it, Date-san.

Kiryu-san. I entrust the secret of Onomichi to you.
At this point, any time I have left is a luxury.

Data from the microfilm my father left me.
Your phone should be able to read it.

And the code you mentioned
to us before is on here?

Indeed. It should prove to be the key
to cracking the secret of Onomichi.

I struggled to solve its mysteries, but one
familiar
 with Onomichi may have more luck.

Be warned, though. The closer you get to the secret
,
the further Hirose will go to stop you.
He'll even kill you if it comes to it.
Why did you choose me for this, though?
You are Haruka Sawamura's guardian.

The father of the girl my son loves. As I see it,
we are the patriarchs of their two families.

Not that I have any right to act as Yuta's
father after everything I've done.

Even so, you are the only one I can trust.
Not just with the secret, but with Yuta as well.
With Yuta?

It seems Yuta has reached the conclusion
that Hirose is a father-figure to him.

It will be difficult for Yuta to continue onward
with this doubt looming over Hirose.
He will require closure of some kind.

And... bringing the secret of Onomichi to light
will provide an opportunity to give it to him.
Wait. I have one more question.

You said before that you don't have much time
left. What did you mean by that?

I've contacted the Saio regarding
 my succession.
Yuta Usami has been dismissed as my heir.

However, that action means that I have
broken the blood law of our organization.

To keep existing, they will have to find a new
leader to take command of the triad.

Furthermore, those who break the blood law
will face a punishment fitting the crime.
Then you're...

A Saio Triad assassin will come to end my life.
Don't worry, I will be far away from you by then.
I also expect the Saio to retreat from Little Asia.

My only regret... is that I couldn't kill Tsuneo Iwami
and bring him to justice for the slaughter of my son.
Lo... Is there anything you want to say to Yuta?
I tried to murder his child.

Even if I tell him how glad I was to finally see
my grandson... I doubt he'll believe me.
Hm? Where's Lo?
Well, I doubt we'll be seeing him again.

Lo, he... He entrusted me with the
key
 to the secret of Onomichi.
So I'm heading to Onomichi now.
Gonna try to figure out the truth?

Yeah. But before I do that, I'll need to
speak to the Hirose Family.

They've idolized Hirose-san as a father
,
but it may come to a showdown with him.

I have to explain things to them.
That's the only fair way to go about this.
I don't see what's in it for you, though.

With Lo out of the picture, nobody'll be trying
to kill Haruka or Haruto anymore.

There's no reason for you to keep poking
around in Onomichi. Is there?

I'm the one who dragged those
Hirose Family guys into this mess.

I can't just abandon them now. They at least
deserve to know what's going on.

Man... You really don't ever change.
Fine, then. Do your worst.

Yuta. I need you to take Haruto
and go be by Haruka's side.
I'll be going to Onomichi alone.

Wh-Whaddaya mean!?
I'm goin' with you!
Listen, Yuta.

Years ago, when Haruka's parents died
before my eyes, I made a promise.

I knew that someday she would fall in love
,
maybe even have a kid.

Until that day came, I promised
to be like a father to her.

Now more than ever,
Haruka needs someone by her side.

That's not a job for her father, though.
It has to be you.
I-I jus' can't do that!

Didn't you hear what Lo said about Hirose-san!?
I won't stand for that bullshit!

That's why I've gotta go to Onomichi too,
and prove the boss is innocent!

And once I manage to do that
I'm gonna kill that asshole Lo for real!
What do you want!?

You got balls to be plotting a murder
in front of a detective. Really?
No, but I didn't...

Yuta Usami. I'm gonna have to question you
about that Little Asia fire down at the station.
H-Hold on a sec!
I'll take care of him.

Us fathers need to stand together. Weird seeing
your daughter get taken away by some punk, huh?
I remember all too well.
Now you're giving <font_kind=yakuza_italic>me</font_kind> lessons?
Let's go, kid.
You've gotta be jokin'!
C'mon! Just lemme go, man!

(Whatever's waiting for me in Onomichi
won't be pretty. I better stock up.)
(I guess I'll grab a taxi when I'm ready.)
(Nagumo and the others should be over at the office.)
Yer Kiryu-san, yeah?

I got a message fer ya from
Chairman Kurusu o' the Yomei Alliance.
He wants y'outta this town, lickety-split.
There a reason?

Cause our boss said so.
That's all the reason y'need.
In that case, I've got no reason to oblige.

We'll do what we gotta do t'get ya gone.
Don't even matter if the sun's still out.

We're done talkin', then.
Y'ready, boys? Fuck him up!
It looks like I have to fight them.

The status of Minoru Daidoji-san remains unknown
with even key advisors apparently still in the dark.

Given his unwillingness to offer interviews
,
we can safely assume his condition is critical.

Daidoji-san was once a high-ranking officer in
the WWII-era navy, but after American occupation...

His influence carried over into
governmental ministries.
